source_read: Morrisons Café menu posters linked from the café page as 'View Menu' and 'View Scottish Menu': https://www.morrisons.com/terms/cafe-menu -> assets.ctfassets.net/um1yk6827v6c/.../5-5-26-cafe-reset-menu-ew.pdf (sha256 42bb1db70a5b50046b35a6bcbb56ae91b246d7d2d023eb2fc275553043bd6829, PDF created 17 April 2026) and https://www.morrisons.com/terms/scottish-cafe-menu -> .../5-5-26-Cafe-Reset-Menu-SCOT.pdf (sha256 3554b794dfcdb8e5699c192c7888c46d28cc4a65fa6047f2f5ab0e05068ebca8); allergen guide https://www.morrisons.com/terms/cafe-allergen-information -> TS01K_Allergen_Information_Guide_Cafe_Menu-28-9-26.pdf (V49, link only); robots.txt of www.morrisons.com allows /terms/, assets.ctfassets.net has no robots.txt (404)
not_verifiable: the exact number of cafés (the café page speaks of 'all of our Cafés' and has a café finder; Morrisons runs several hundred supermarkets)
notes: Extractor: word boxes (pdftotext -bbox-layout) with a dish->anchor table in which every one of the 122 'NNNkcal' words on the E&W poster (the footer 'Adults need around 2000kcal' excepted, sauce figures in brackets inside descriptions excepted) is claimed by exactly one dish. Independent check: every published item's calories found again in the poster's plain pdftotext -layout text on or just under the line holding the dish's printed words (113 automatically, Goodfella's Mac & Cheese & Garlic Bread (kids) 685 kcal by eye: its figure sits far right on the same layout line), and the 25 dishes read 'below' or 'right' of their name were compared by eye with the coordinate dump. Fixed in the script: veggie sausages had been tagged pork from the word 'sausage', and 'with butter or vegan spread' had tagged toast and rolls vegetarian. Left out: 8 breakfast dishes that the Scottish menu prints under the same name with different calories (its recipes add tattie scones and lorne sausage: Full Veggie 937 vs 1071, Full Vegan 789 vs 923, Big Breakfast Roll/Wrap, Veggie Roll/Wrap, Vegan Roll/Wrap), never chosen between; 10 Scotland-only dishes (regional). No alcoholic drinks on either poster.
